newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil judge orders suspension of CVRD selloff.
newsitem.headline: Brazil judge orders suspension of CVRD selloff.

text.p: A Brazilian judge has ordered that next week's scheduled privatization of mining conglomerate Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) be suspended, a Planning Ministry spokeswoman said.
Government lawyers would appeal against the decision, which was taken in a court in Sao Paulo, and hoped to reverse the ruling as soon as possible, the spokeswoman said.
"This doesn't mean the privatization has been called off," the spokeswoman said. "The government is appealing and if it wins, the sale goes ahead as planned. If not, then we'll have to suspend it."

The government plans to auction 45 percent of CVRD's voting capital April 29 on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange, the first step in what is set to become Latin America's biggest privatization with receipts seen over $5.0 billion.
Dozens of court cases have been filed against the sale of CVRD in courts across the country. Until now, no injunctions suspending the sale of the company had been granted.
The judge who issued Friday's injunction, Joao Batista Goncalves, said the case had been brought by a group of individuals led by a Sao Paulo university professor.

The group alleged irregularities in the bid specifications which set down the rules for the privatization of CVRD and that the government had not presented a "convincing case" for the sale, the judge told Reuters.

Goncalves said that while he had the power to revoke the injunction, the government's appeal would be sent to another court. He also said he was due to study another, separate request for an injunction against the CVRD sale.
